clue.text: Incidental benefit for each is put in fairly

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'ten pounds per head'

indicators.note: the word is goes into the middle of the synonym for fairly

parts.note: fairly means quite, as in 'quite good'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told a side benefit is shared out fairly to each person.
explanation.definitionFit: A perk, formally the longer word, is a bonus received on top of regular pay.

clue.text: Collected short cape in tartan material

indicators.note: the shortened cape sits inside the word for tartan cloth

parts.note: plaid is cloth woven in a tartan pattern
C is the map abbreviation for Cape

explanation.surface: A composed figure wears a cropped cape made of tartan.
explanation.definitionFit: A collected person is calm and self-possessed, which is exactly what placid means.

clue.text: Confirm swimmer in ocean is holding up well

indicators.note: the sea creature's name wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish found swimming in the sea

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for well is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: fit means well, in good health

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that a fish in the ocean is keeping up its health.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratify a treaty or decision is to approve it formally, giving it official sanction.

clue.text: Unique, unlike bar used by gymnast

definitions.meaning: one of a kind, matched by nothing else
read jokily as not like the twin bars on which a gymnast performs

explanation.surface: Something one of a kind is unlike the apparatus a gymnast uses.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as UN- (not) plus PARALLELED, as if meaning 'not resembling the parallel bars' of gymnastics.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without equal or precedent is one of a kind, without any match.

clue.text: Channel port, for example

definitions.meaning: a TV channel is informally a ..., as in 'switch over to the other ...'
port is the left-hand ... of a ship

explanation.surface: A harbour town on the English Channel is offered as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel port' reads as one phrase, like Dover or Calais, but it splits into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcasting station was once called a side in Britain, and port names the left flank of a vessel.

clue.text: Working group briefly found in front of VW

definitions.text: briefly found in front of VW
definitions.meaning: the short form of the answer is two letters that stand just before V and W in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A team of workers is hastily spotted in front of a Volkswagen car.
explanation.walkthrough: VW looks like the car maker, but it is just the letters V and W; the abbreviation TU comes right before them in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A labour organisation of workers bargaining collectively for pay and conditions.

clue.text: An edible tuber brought back, one native to south America

indicators.note: the phrase 'an edible tuber' is turned around and read backwards

parts.note: a yam is a starchy root vegetable eaten in the tropics

explanation.surface: An edible root vegetable is brought home, a crop native to South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The Maya people actually belong to Central America (Mexico, Guatemala, Belize), so the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayan people are an indigenous population of the Americas, famed for their ancient civilisation.

clue.text: Goodbye to sarkozy

parts.note: the farewell one would say in French to the former French president Nicolas Sarkozy

explanation.surface: Bidding farewell to the former French president.
explanation.definitionFit: The French farewell phrase literally means until we see again.

clue.text: Leaders of the econuts embraced by al gore, perhaps, or another personality

indicators.note: the opening letters sit inside the name before it is reworked
the letters are only a possible arrangement of the politician's name, to be reworked
the opening letters of the two words the and econuts

explanation.surface: Green activists' chiefs are hugged by the environmentalist former US vice president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ALGORE once the T and E (the first letters of 'the econuts') are put inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A second self, a different side of someone's character, sometimes taken as a separate identity.

clue.text: Directly opposite to a silly point by churchman

indicators.note: silly suggests the word point is jumbled foolishly

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman in charge of a cathedral

explanation.surface: In cricket, a fielder at silly point stands near a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: Silly point is a cricket fielding position very close to the batter, which disguises 'silly' as part of a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Places at opposite ends of the globe, diametrically across the Earth, are described with this adjective.

clue.text: Jester hiding king's document from court

indicators.note: the comic figure's word conceals the royal letter inside it

parts.note: a wit is someone who makes jokes
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A court jester conceals the king's paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal legal order issued by a judge or tribunal.

clue.text: Party time with diamonds, say — and nothing to wear

parts.note: a birthday is an occasion for a party
diamonds is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone getting ready for a party with jewels finds they have no clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds' suggests jewellery for the party, but it is a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked, as on the day you were born, is the humorous idiom.

clue.text: Communicate knowledge to popular class

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: A teacher shares knowledge with a well-liked group of pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell someone facts or to notify them is to pass information along.

clue.text: Live with deception by extremely limited adherent

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live
a lie is a deception

indicators.note: limited means the synonym for extremely is cut short at its end

parts.note: very means extremely

explanation.surface: A follower lives amid lies, only to a very modest extent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' trims the last letter off VERY to give VER.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of a faith or cause holds its convictions with faith.

clue.text: Deceive female I spotted with poet, a close friend

parts.note: to con is to deceive
Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A woman is spotted with a poet, deceiving everyone about their friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman to whom one tells secrets and private matters, a trusted intimate.

clue.text: Rejecting compromise, liberal or no, in island parliament

indicators.note: the three short pieces are placed within the name of the parliament

parts.note: the Althing is the parliament of Iceland
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Liberal member of an island's parliament refuses to compromise, whether he gets support or not.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncompromising choice demanding everything or else accepting zero.

clue.text: Husband trapped by murderer spotted tool used in gory massacre

indicators.note: the husband's letter is caught inside the murderer's name

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in the Bible
saw is the past tense of see, meaning spotted

explanation.surface: A husband caught by a killer sees the weapon from a gory slaying.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the horror film The Texas Chain Saw Massacre.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor-driven cutting device with teeth on a loop, famous from a horror film title.

clue.text: Count rat, possibly, as this

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of count rat could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An aristocrat who betrays his side might be called a rat.
explanation.walkthrough: As an &lit, the whole clue is the definition: a count who ratted would be one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor who switches sides is called a rat, the slang for a deserter.

clue.text: Pub for proverbially drunk types, or the other place

definitions.meaning: a house is a pub, and 'drunk as a lord' is the proverb, so a house for lords
MPs in the Commons call the upper chamber the other place

explanation.surface: A tavern for heavy drinkers is somewhere else entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: The British upper house of parliament is referred to in the House of Commons as 'the other place'.
explanation.definitionFit: The second chamber of the UK Parliament, a pub for peers on the jokey reading.

clue.text: A wife found in one African country or another

indicators.note: the article and the abbreviation for wife are placed inside the country's name

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A wife has settled in some African country or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the definition: another African country, following on from Mali.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked state in south-east Africa, so it is a second African nation here.

clue.text: Livingstone uplifted no African native

parts.note: Ken Livingstone was the first Mayor of London

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifted means the word for no is read from bottom to top

parts.note: nay means no

explanation.surface: The explorer Livingstone, lifted up, says no to an African native.
explanation.walkthrough: Livingstone suggests David the explorer of Africa, but it is Ken Livingstone, the London politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born in Kenya, the East African nation.

clue.text: Purpose concealed by corrupt union — that's the insinuation

indicators.note: the synonym for purpose goes inside the jumbled word
corrupt means the letters of union are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: A dishonest trade union hides its real aims, which is the implication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' turns UNION into INNUO; 'concealed by' then signals the aim being tucked inside, with the surface's dodgy trade union a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A sly hint or suggestive remark, an indirect suggestion, often rude.

clue.text: Acceptance of captain's order I repeatedly proclaimed

indicators.note: repeatedly tells us the single letter I is given twice over
proclaimed means the letters are spoken out loud, giving a sound

parts.note: the letter I, spoken, is the word for yes used at sea

explanation.surface: A sailor loudly declares they accept the captain's command again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: The naval phrase a sailor says to acknowledge and agree to an instruction.

clue.text: Highest level of excellent service on both sides of motorway

indicators.note: the tennis word sits either side of the road letter

parts.note: an ace is an unreturnable serve in tennis
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Top-quality service stations line both sides of the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests motorway service stations, but service is a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: The peak or summit, the point of greatest perfection.

clue.text: Betray in hush-hush operation

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words hush-hush operation

explanation.surface: A traitor sells out others in a secret mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word, but it signals letters concealed across the end of 'hush' and the start of 'operation'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to inform on someone to the police is to grass or rat on them.

clue.text: Error seen in a key position of church

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
C is a musical key
a curacy is the post held by a curate in the church

explanation.surface: A mistake is spotted in an important church appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key position' reads as important post, but key is the musical key C.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake or lack of precision.

clue.text: This inventor said what?

indicators.note: said means the word what is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the question word itself

explanation.surface: Someone asks 'what?' and an inventor is announced.
explanation.walkthrough: James Watt was the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine.
explanation.definitionFit: James Watt was a Scottish engineer whose improved steam engine powered the Industrial Revolution.

clue.text: Boring regurgitation of pedantries

indicators.note: regurgitation means the word pedantries is thrown back up in a different order

explanation.surface: Pedants repeating their nit-picking is dreary.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and uninspired, lacking any imagination or flair.
